title: 2.7.1 Individual PA Part 1: Concepts and Traces
description: Eight questions: three on the ideas of Chapter 2, five where you read a short program and say what it prints. One submission, nothing marked on screen.

questions.question: The condition inside if (...) is not required to be a comparison. What does if actually do with whatever is inside the parentheses?
options: It converts it to true or false, using the six falsy values
It requires a comparison and refuses anything else
It runs the condition and checks whether the line printed true
It treats the line as text and checks whether it spells true
questions.explanation: if converts whatever is inside the parentheses to a boolean (2.1.18). Zero, an empty string, null, undefined, NaN and false convert to false; everything else converts to true. That is why if (x == true) is redundant when x is already a boolean -- if (x) does the same job.

questions.question: A switch statement is deciding which case to run. How does it compare the value against each case label?
options: With strict equality (===), so a string "4" never matches the number 4
With loose equality (==), converting types to find a match
It converts every case label to text before comparing
By treating a quoted case label as a different type from the value
questions.explanation: switch matches with strict equality (2.3.18). switch (4) never matches case "4": the number 4 and the text "4" are different values under ===, which is exactly why a value of the wrong type falls through to default.

questions.question: A loop sits inside another loop. The outer one runs 3 times. On every pass of the outer loop, the inner one runs 2 times. How many times does the inner loop's body run in total?
questions.explanation: Every pass of the outer loop runs the inner loop start to finish, so the inner body runs 3 x 2 = 6 times (2.4.24). Nested-loop cost is the product, not the sum.

questions.explanation: Loose equality converts before comparing: false becomes the number 0, and 0 == 0 is true, so the if runs and prints empty. That is the == trap; === would compare the boolean against the number and say false.
